did_you_know.text: Did you know? Proverbs 11 opens by condemning dishonest scales: using unfair measures is described as an abomination to the Lord, while an honest measure is pleasing to Him.
Did you know? The chapter contrasts pride with humility: pride brings disgrace, while the humble are described as gaining wisdom.

Did you know? According to the verse, wealth is of no benefit on the day of wrath, but righteousness can deliver a person from death. Thus, the chapter emphasizes the value of righteousness beyond material possessions.
Did you know? The chapter warns of the destructive power of a deceitful mouth, which can ruin one's neighbor, while knowledge can help deliver the righteous.

Did you know? Proverbs teaches that a nation may fall when there is no guidance or wise counsel, but deliverance comes through an abundance of counselors. The verse emphasizes the importance of sound advice in leading a community.
Did you know? The chapter presents kindness as a way of benefiting oneself: whoever shows kindness to others is described as a kind person, while the cruel person harms himself.

Did you know? Physical beauty alone is not presented as a sufficient virtue: a beautiful woman who lacks discretion is compared to a gold ring in a pig's snout—something precious in a place where it does not belong.
Did you know? One of the chapter's proverbs presents a surprising principle: some people give generously and gain even more, while those who withhold what is right end up in poverty.
Did you know? The generous person and the one who refreshes others are described as being refreshed themselves. The verse connects generosity toward others with abundance and blessing.

Did you know? The chapter calls the fruit of the righteous an “tree of life” and attributes wisdom to the one who wins souls. In this way, it portrays the beneficial influence of a righteous and wise person on others.
